outcome: positive neonatal polymerase chain reaction (for COVID-19)
cohort: A total of 210 hospitalized pregnant women (70 with confirmed COVID-19 and 140 COVID-negative controls matched by age and parity) and their newborns were evaluated.
finding: COVID-19 infection during pregnancy was associated with increased maternal complications (preeclampsia, preterm labor, fetal distress, reduced fetal movements, cesarean delivery, non-reactive non-stress test) and adverse neonatal outcomes (lower birth weight, respiratory distress, NICU admission, gastrointestinal issues, feeding problems, fever, and positive PCR).
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was significantly more common in pregnant women with confirmed COVID-19 infection.
